entries.name: Gen 3 Box
entries.tagline: Storage as a Ruby and Sapphire style grid you can search, sort and mark.
entries.description: A Ruby/Sapphire-style storage screen over Gen 1's twelve boxes of twenty: a visible 5x4 grid drawn from the per-species battle pics, a cursor that picks a Pokemon up and puts it down, swapping on an occupied slot, and SELECT to cross between the box and the party. Search every box by species, type, or mark with FIND; sort by dex, level, name, or type with UNDO; mark Pokemon with the four Gen 3 symbols; give each box a custom name up to eight glyphs and pick a wallpaper from six patterns; and hear a cry every time a Pokemon lands. BOX HEALS rests everything in storage when you close the screen. GRID BIG doubles the surface to 320x288, showing battle pics at full size and giving each Pokemon its own species palette. OW SPRITES (on by default) draws Wilds of Kanto's overworld sprites in the CLASSIC grid when that mod is installed. It runs on Gold as well as on Red, Blue and Yellow: Gen 2's fourteen boxes, its split Special, its own summary screen and its MAIL rules are all honoured.

entries.name: Gen 3 Dex
entries.tagline: The Pokedex as a grid of pictures, every owned species in its own colours.
entries.description: The Pokedex as a grid of pictures instead of a list of names. Owned species wear their own palette -- twenty-one colours at once where the Game Boy could show four -- seen-but-uncaught are dimmed, and the rest are blanks. SELECT filters to OWNED, MISSING or SEEN ONLY. A offers DATA / CRY / AREA like the vanilla list -- AREA is the engine's own nest map, which blinks every place the species lives. DATA goes to the engine's own species page, so Useful Dex's extra pages still work. Runs on Gold too: fourteen rows of Johto instead of stopping at Mew, the caught half of the dex read where Gold keeps it, DATA/AREA routed to Gold's own dex entry, and GRID BIG now draws its full 320x288 grid there as well, through Gold's own widescreen contract -- without the per-species palette zones, which stay a Super Game Boy trick Gold has no use for.

entries.name: Groovy Palette & Frames
entries.tagline: Thirty more colour schemes and eight text box borders, previewed on the running game.
entries.description: Thirty more entries on the COLORS row -- Amiga Workbench, the C64 boot screen, a Virtual Boy, rainbow, fuchsia, vaporwave -- plus eight new borders for every text box and menu. Press A on OPTION -> COLORS (or, on Gold, OPTION -> COLOR) and the menu lifts off the game: the palette name and nothing else, left and right to walk the list, previewed on the running game. USE ADVANCED rides the engine's own per-tile colorization instead of replacing it -- the pokered-gbc pack on Red/Blue/Yellow, Gold's own GBC palettes on Gold -- so a palette recolours dozens of colours on screen rather than four. The FRAME half works identically on both generations, through the same Font.drawBox both draw their boxes with; the palette half now does too, riding Gold's own GbcPalette.resolve the same way it rides PaletteFX.effectiveColors on Gen 1. The one gap: Gold's title screen and Gold/Silver boot cinema keep their own pre-rendered art (the same boundary its DMG and CLASSIC color modes already live with) and pick up the scheme from the first menu or map onward.

entries.tagline: Hold B to move faster, at a speed you choose, with a trail off your heels.
entries.description: Hold B to walk faster, at a speed you pick: x1.5, x2, x3 or x4. Rides the engine's own movement.speed hook, whose comment names running shoes as the reason it exists. A run can leave a trail off your heels -- smoke, flames or lightning -- reaching about three and a half cells back; it can CUT the tall grass you run across, one clod at a time, the way the CUT move cuts it, so that grass has no Pokemon left in it; and it can carry you through tall grass without ever starting a wild battle. Every one of those has an off switch, the last two ship off, and with all three left alone nothing but the duration of a step changes. Optional boosts for the bicycle and for surfing too. Runs on Pokemon Gold too, and as of 1.6.0 every row works there: RUN SPEED, BOOST BIKE, BOOST SURF, SAFE GRASS, CUT GRASS and RUN FX all cross over. 1.7.0 adds the Dramatic Shape voxel mod's first- and third-person cameras, which replace the grid walk with a continuous one and used to leave every row of this mod silent; the speed, CUT GRASS and SAFE GRASS all work inside them now. entries.name: Kanto Companion
entries.tagline: A controller friendly overlay built for a small screen: party, route encounters and battle matchups on one button, items and boxes on another.
entries.description: Overhaul designed to optimize display on a smaller screen and for use with a controller. An in-game companion. Press R2 to toggle a live overlay (party, trainer, route encounters, and a battle matchup screen during fights). Press X for an Items screen to move items between your Bag and the PC (drag/click, quantities, sort). Press Y for a Party/Boxes screen to deposit, withdraw, rearrange and swap Pokemon by drag-and-drop. Press F6 (or R3 on a controller) to enter Edit Mode and freely drag, resize, and collapse every panel to fit your screen exactly how you want it, with full mouse/touch/gamepad support and settings that persist across sessions. NEW: if a compatible weather mod is installed (e.g. Weather FX), the Route panel shows live weather-adjusted encounter odds and weather-only species instead of the static base table, plus a current-weather readout next to every location's name. Nothing changes without one installed. Enforces the game's limits (box/bag caps; the party is never left without a healthy Pokemon). Fan-made; not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo / Game Freak / The Pokemon Company.

entries.name: Move Type Fixes
entries.tagline: Gust flies and Karate Chop fights, the way Gen 2 corrected them, so the Pokemon that learn them finally get their STAB.
entries.description: Gust becomes Flying and Karate Chop becomes Fighting, the way Gen 2 corrected them, so the Pokemon that learn them get the STAB they should have had. Sand-Attack to Ground is a separate toggle, off by default, since a Ground move cannot touch Flying. Also keeps Gen 1's Ghost 0x Psychic matchup, overriding mods that patch it out. Bite stays Normal: Gen 1 has no Dark type.

entries.name: Species Rebalance
entries.tagline: Dragon moves worth using, fixed stats on 17 Pokemon, retyped Gengar and Charizard, and learnsets they should always have had, each behind its own switch.
entries.description: Gen 1 only has one Dragon move and it does a flat 40 damage, so Dragon types never really got to play like one. This adds Twister, Dragonbreath and a physical Outrage. It also fixes stats on 17 Pokemon, retypes Gengar, Pinsir and Charizard, gives Arcanine and Ninetales the learnsets they never had, and lets Charizard learn Fly. Everything is switchable, and the two biggest changes ship switched off.

entries.name: Stronger Trainers
entries.tagline: Gym leaders, rivals and the Elite Four field full teams of six with real type coverage, and switch when the matchup turns against them.
entries.description: Gym leaders, the Elite Four, the Champion, the rivals and Giovanni field full six-Pokemon teams with real type coverage, on a level curve computed from the experience a playthrough actually banks rather than guessed at. Bosses switch to answer a bad matchup, and a fair-play AI estimates damage and weighs accuracy. Red, Blue and Yellow each get their own rosters, so Yellow's rival fights his own Eevee line at the right levels. Every ordinary trainer gets a level bump and stops fielding pre-evolutions its level has outgrown. The static overworld encounters are raised to match, and the legendary birds sit at level 70 with movesets to go with it. All adjustable from the MODS menu.

entries.name: Gym Leader Shuffle

entries.description: Standalone Gym Leader Shuffle for Kanto and Johto in Gold and Silver, with optional Crystal 251 compatibility. No randomizer or starter mod is required; each physical gym keeps its own badge, rewards, progression, and level curve.

entries.name: Color Saturation
entries.tagline: One dial from 0 to 150 percent that makes the game more or less colourful without shifting a single hue.
entries.description: One SATURATION dial, 0 to 150 percent, that scales how colourful the game is without changing the colours. Every palette that tones ADVANCED down does it by dragging every hue toward one family -- sepia warm, ocean cool, pocket grey. This scales each colour's distance from grey instead, so luminance and hue stay exactly where they were and only chroma moves: 70 is ADVANCED with the shouting turned down, 0 is a true greyscale of the real colours, 150 is louder than vanilla.

entries.name: Pokeball Colorfix
entries.tagline: Colours the Poke Balls the game leaves grey: the ball you throw, the party rows beside your team, and the healing machine.
entries.description: Colors the Poke Balls the game leaves gray: the thrown ball in battle (fixed per-ball palette -- red Poke, blue Great, gold Ultra, purple Master, green Safari, instead of sampling the enemy Pokemon's colors), the party ball rows per state (red healthy, amber statused, dimmed fainted), and the Pokemon Center healing machine. Also turns on colorization for the battle animation layer under the WIDE layout, which skips it entirely.

entries.name: Pokemove Colorfix
entries.tagline: Move animations in the colour of their type: Ember burns orange, Thundershock is yellow, Surf is blue.
entries.description: Battle move animations render two-tone white-and-black because their sprites use the f0 OBJ palette slot, which selects only the lightest and darkest shades -- the hue is discarded before any palette is consulted, so no COLORS mod can reach it. This gives every move animation a three-stop ramp from its elemental type: Ember burns orange, Thundershock is yellow, Surf is blue. Fifteen type ramps plus a small per-move exception list, all editable at the top of main.lua.

entries.name: Stadium 2 Overworld Models (Gold and Silver)
entries.tagline: Gold and Silver in 3D: a voxel Johto, Stadium 2 models for all 251, a follower that walks behind you, and a Stadium style battle UI.
entries.description: A standalone 3D overhaul for Gold and Silver. It rebuilds Johto as voxel terrain with day and night lighting, renders party and wild Pokemon as Stadium 2 models extracted from a Stadium 2 cartridge you supply yourself, and gives the overworld a follower that tracks whichever Pokemon sits at the top of your party. Battles, the Pokedex and the pause menus get a Stadium style glass UI with a controller command diamond, and OPEN WORLD zoom pulls the camera back over the whole region. First person and free camera modes are included, and it coexists with the 3D Character Selector. Nothing here needs another mod installed first: the voxel and roaming Wilds runtimes travel inside the package.
